doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: London House, George Shearing's snub and the Round Table with Mel Torme
summary: Shearing would not share the London House bill with her; at the Round Table she opened for Mel Torme before a more sophisticated cabaret audience.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Some of the other venues, the London House in Chicago?
That was a good one. They had blueberry muffins there. He didn’t want to play on the bill with me.
George Shearing. They wanted to put me on the bill, he said, “Uh-uhhh, I don’t know her.” They put in Barbara Carroll or someone like that.
The Round Table in New York.
I played there with Mel Torme.
Was Mel performing with you on the same bill?
Would you open or would you close?
Were there differences between the audience at The Round Table and The Embers?
Different kind of crowd? How so?
The audiences at The Round Table were more sophisticated. They’re cabaret-ers.
In playing to that audience, what would you play differently than you would play at The Embers?
